title: Online Auction System
summary: Design an online auction platform where many users bid in real time and the highest bid wins at the deadline.
statement: Design an auction system like eBay. Sellers list items with an end time; buyers place bids that must beat the current price; the system picks a winner at the deadline and handles last-second bidding fairly. Start by clarifying requirements and estimating scale, then design the system and defend your decisions.
initialGuidance: Clarify the users, the main journeys, and what is explicitly out of scope before drawing anything.
Estimate read and write volume and storage growth; the numbers decide which components you need.
Name the guarantees you will offer (consistency, durability, availability) and the trade-offs behind them.
Write down assumptions as you make them and revisit them when requirements change.
coreFunctionalRequirements: List items with an auction end time.
Place bids higher than the current bid.
Show live current price to watchers.
Close auctions at the deadline and pick a winner.
Notify bidders of outbid and win events.

requirementQuestions.question: Must bid ordering be strict, and what decides ties?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Selects between strong and eventual models and shapes conflict handling.

requirementQuestions.question: How many active auctions, bids per second, and watchers per hot auction?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Sets read and write rates and storage growth, which decide whether a single node can cope.

requirementQuestions.question: How quickly must price updates reach watchers?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Defines which paths need caching, precomputation, or regional placement.

requirementQuestions.question: Are auto-bids (proxy bidding) and anti-sniping extensions supported?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Fixes what is in and out of the design so effort goes to what matters.

requirementQuestions.question: How are shill bidding and fake bids detected?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Adds validation, rate limiting, and fraud controls to the critical path.

requirementQuestions.question: What proof of bids is required for disputes?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines the data model, retention, and storage choices.

workloadAssumptions.illustrativeNote: All numbers below are illustrative examples for practice and are not benchmarks. Real answers depend on the requirements the candidate negotiates.

estimationPrompts: What is the bid rate for one hot auction at the deadline?
How many price update pushes per second does this create?
How many timers must fire per second at peak?

keyDecisions.question: How are concurrent bids ordered?
considerations: Serialise bids per auction through a single partition owner.

keyDecisions.question: How are auctions closed reliably?
considerations: Timers or scheduled jobs trigger closing.
A bid arriving at the boundary uses server time.

keyDecisions.question: How do watchers see changes?
considerations: Pub/sub with push over WebSockets or server-sent events.

keyDecisions.question: How are automatic bids handled?
considerations: Store maximum bids server-side and increment minimally.

tradeoffs.tension: Per-auction ordering limits parallelism for hot items.

commonMistakes: Closing auctions with a once-per-minute scan.
No durable record of every bid.
followUps: How do you handle a hot auction with 100,000 watchers?
How do you prevent shill bidding?
How do you implement a Dutch auction?
How would you handle seller cancellation?
